newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt gets 15 prequalification bids for BOT roads.
newsitem.headline: Egypt gets 15 prequalification bids for BOT roads.

text.p: Fifteen companies are vying to prequalify to build four highways in Egypt under a build, operate and transfer (BOT) formula, the state's General Authority for Roads and Bridges said on Thursday.
Essam al-Darawi, assistant manager at the authority, said the authority would decide in five weeks which firms were eligible to tender for building 1,850 km (1,150 miles) of highways.
The contractors will build the roads from their own resources and charge tolls for a fixed period, after which ownership will revert to the state.
"Companies from Egypt, the Arab world, Europe and the United States have submitted prequalification documents," Darawi said.

He said they included French firm Bouygues and Kuwaiti firm Mohamed Abdulmuhsin Kharafi and Sons, which has also bid to build another BOT project -- an airport at Marsa Alam on the Red Sea coast expected to cost about 120 million pounds ($35 million).

The four planned highways will link Alexandria to the oasis of Fayoum southwest of Cairo 240 km (150 miles) away; from Fayoum the 850 km (530 miles) to the southern town to Aswan; from Deirut in the southern province of Assiut 260 km (160 miles) to the western oasis of Farafra and from Kharga oasis to Oweinat 500 km (310 miles) away in the far southwest of the country
The government has also offered private investors airports and power plants under the BOT formula. The most advanced project is the Marsa Alam airport.
